key_insight: AIR teaches multimodal LLMs to adaptively switch between reasoning and code during complex numerical tasks, improving interleaved reasoning beyond vision-only tool use.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a practical reinforcement-learning recipe for building more reliable MLLM agents that can decide when to invoke code for computation-heavy problems.
method: Two-stage cold-start data construction to bootstrap interleaved reasoning trajectories.
Data filtering for curating RL training samples.
Adaptive tool invocation with a group-constrained reward function for trajectory-level reinforcement learning.
evidence_signal: After RL with the group-constrained reward, average benchmark performance improved by 6.1 pp, interleaved reasoning accuracy rose by 9.9 pp, and tool-use success exceeded 95%.
watch_item: Results depend on carefully curated RL data and reward design, so generalization may be sensitive to task distribution and tool-invocation formatting.
paper_title: AIR: Adaptive Interleaved Reasoning with Code in MLLMs
